To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the preprocessing of MS/ML spectra can significantly increase the sensitivity of database search without compromising its specificity and that a preprocessing method based on the removal of low intensity peaks, which are likely to be spurious, can be used to reduce the size and complexity of the input data set.

(i) preprocessing MS/MS spectra with the software MSFitter can increase peptide identification by 10–20% at reduced file sizes; (ii) MSFitter is the best preprocessing method in terms of sensitivity, specificity and run‐time; (iii) MSFitter can reduce the number of false positive peptide identifications; (iv) MSFitter outperforms other preprocessing methods, including X!

(i) the preprocessing methods that are currently available are not optimal for the identification of low‐abundance peptides, (ii) preprocessing methods that are specifically designed to identify low‐abundance proteins perform better than general purpose methods and (iii) the combination of several preprocessing methods can yield better results than any single method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient and robust methods to preprocess MS/MS spectra.

(1) the identification of the best preprocessing methods for MS/MS data, (2) the identification of preprocessing parameters that are most relevant for peptide identification, and (3) the identification of parameters that are not relevant for peptide identification.

the following topics: (1) The development of a software tool for the efficient preprocessing of MS spectra (2) The evaluation of 25 preprocessing methods for their effectiveness and computational efficiency (3) A comparison of the performance of 3 database search algorithms (4) An evaluation of the performance of the preprocessing methods on the different search algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single preprocessing method is superior to all others.
the choice of a specific preprocessing algorithm is dependent on the type of data and the type of analysis that is to be performed.
the best preprocessing method depends on the data set and the search engine used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a) preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra is essential to increase the sensitivity and specificity of peptide identification, b) a combination of several preprocessing algorithms yields the highest sensitivity for peptide identification, and c) a preprocessing method that combines a number of different methods, such as the one we present here, can be a powerful alternative to the use of more sophisticated database search algorithms, especially when the latter are computationally expensive.
the preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra can be very effective for improving peptide identification.
the preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra can be a valuable tool to improve the sensitivity of database search algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preprocessing of MS/ MS spectra is a crucial step in peptide identification.

preprocessing MS/MS spectra is a valuable step in the analysis pipeline, which can be used to improve peptide identification and reduce the number of false positives, while reducing the number of false negatives.
preprocessing MS/MS spectra with the following steps is sufficient: (i) peak picking; (ii) de‐isotoping; (iii) de‐convolution; (iv) smoothing and (v) baseline subtraction.
